summary: The two loaves of Shavuos are kneaded and baked one at a time. The lechem hapanim is kneaded one at a time and baked two at a time, in a mold, and put back into a mold after baking so it keeps its shape.

chunks.en: The two loaves are kneaded one at a time,
chunks.st: The two loaves that are brought on the festival of Shavuot from the new wheat are each made from a tenth of an ephah of fine flour. They are kneaded one by one

chunks.en: and baked one at a time.
chunks.st: and they are baked one by one, i.e., each loaf is placed separately in the oven.

chunks.en: The lechem hapanim is kneaded one at a time,
chunks.st: The loaves of the shewbread are kneaded one by one

chunks.en: and baked two at a time.
chunks.st: and baked two by two, i.e., two loaves are placed in the oven at the same time.

chunks.en: And he would make them in a mold.
chunks.st: And the baker would prepare the shewbread in a mold [defus] when he made the dough.

chunks.en: And when he takes them out of the oven,
chunks.st: When he removes the shewbread from the oven

chunks.en: he puts them in a mold,
chunks.st: he again places the loaves in a mold

chunks.en: so that they will not get ruined.
chunks.st: so that their shape will not be ruined.

summary: The two loaves and the lechem hapanim are kneaded and shaped outside the courtyard and baked inside, and their making does not push aside Shabbos. Rabbi Yehuda says everything is done inside. Rabbi Shimon says they are kosher whether made in the courtyard or in Beis Pagi.

chunks.he: אֶחָד שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְאֶחָד לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
chunks.en: Both the two loaves and the lechem hapanim:
chunks.st: In the case of both the two loaves and the shewbread,

chunks.en: their kneading and shaping are outside,
chunks.st: the kneading of their dough and the forming of their loaves take place outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: and their baking is inside,
chunks.st: but their baking takes place inside the Temple courtyard.

chunks.en: and they do not push aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: And their preparation does not override Shabbat.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: All their work is done inside.
chunks.st: All of the procedures involved in their preparation take place inside the courtyard.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: Always be used to saying:
chunks.st: One should always be accustomed to say that

chunks.he: שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים כְּשֵׁרוֹת בָּעֲזָרָה,
chunks.en: The two loaves and the lechem hapanim are kosher in the courtyard,
chunks.st: the two loaves and the shewbread are fit if they were prepared in the Temple courtyard

chunks.en: and kosher in Beis Pagi.
chunks.st: and they are also fit if they were prepared in Beit Pagei,
chunks.stMore: outside the Temple Mount, as he maintains that they may be baked outside the Temple courtyard.

words.note: A place outside the Har HaBayis.

summary: The Kohen Gadol's griddle-cakes are kneaded, shaped and baked inside the courtyard, and this pushes aside Shabbos, but grinding and sifting the flour do not. Rabbi Akiva's rule: work that could be done before Shabbos does not push aside Shabbos.

chunks.en: The griddle-cakes of the Kohen Gadol:
chunks.st: With regard to the twelve loaves of the High Priest’s griddle-cake offering, of which six are offered in the morning and six in the evening,

chunks.en: their kneading, shaping and baking are inside,
chunks.st: their kneading, the forming of their loaves, and their baking take place inside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: and they push aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: and all types of labor involved in those actions override Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: These labors cannot be performed prior to Shabbat, as once the loaves are consecrated in a service vessel they are disqualified if they are left overnight.

chunks.he: טִחוּנָן וְהֶרְקֵדָן אֵינָן דּוֹחוֹת אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
chunks.en: Their grinding and sifting do not push aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: Grinding their flour and sifting their flour do not override Shabbat.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said a rule:
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva stated a principle:

chunks.en: Any work that can
chunks.st: Any labor that can

chunks.en: be done before Shabbos
chunks.st: be performed on Shabbat eve

chunks.en: does not push aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: does not override Shabbat, but

chunks.he: וְשֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהּ לֵעָשׂוֹת מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: And work that cannot be done before Shabbos
chunks.st: one that cannot be performed on Shabbat eve

chunks.en: pushes aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: overrides Shabbat.

summary: Work on menachos done inside the courtyard uses a holy vessel; work done outside does not. The mishnah gives the size of the two loaves and the lechem hapanim, with Rabbi Yehuda's memory trick. Ben Zoma explains that the lechem hapanim had flat "faces" (sides).

chunks.he: כָּל הַמְּנָחוֹת יֵשׁ בָּהֶן מַעֲשֵׂה כְלִי בִּפְנִים,
chunks.en: All the menachos that are worked on inside are made in a holy vessel,
chunks.st: All preparatory procedures of the meal offerings that take place inside the Temple courtyard, e.g., kneading and forming the High Priest’s griddle cakes, involve the use of a service vessel that consecrates the offerings.

chunks.en: but those worked on outside are not made in a holy vessel.
chunks.st: But any preparatory procedures that take place outside the Temple courtyard, e.g., kneading and forming the two loaves and the shewbread, do not involve the use of a service vessel.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם אָרְכָּן שִׁבְעָה וְרָחְבָּן אַרְבָּעָה,
chunks.en: How? The two loaves are seven tefachim long and four wide,
chunks.st: With regard to the two loaves, their length is seven handbreadths, their width is four handbreadths, and

chunks.en: and their horns are four fingers high.
chunks.st: they have hornlike protrusions made of dough that is attached to each of their corners, which are four fingerbreadths high.

words.note: Pieces of dough sticking up at the corners.

chunks.en: The lechem hapanim:
chunks.st: With regard to the loaves of shewbread,

chunks.en: they are ten tefachim long and five wide,
chunks.st: their length is ten handbreadths, their width is five handbreadths, and

chunks.en: and its horns are seven fingers high.
chunks.st: each loaf’s hornlike protrusions is seven fingerbreadths high.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: So that you will not make a mistake,
chunks.st: The following letters are a mnemonic so that you will not err and forget the dimensions of the two loaves:

chunks.en: remember zayin-dalet-dalet and yud-hei-zayin.
chunks.explain: The letters stand for the numbers 7-4-4 and 10-5-7.
chunks.st: Zayin, dalet, dalet. The numerical value of the letter zayin is seven and the numerical value of the letter dalet is four. The mnemonic therefore represents the length of seven handbreadths, the width of four handbreadths, and the height of four fingerbreadths, respectively. The following letters are a mnemonic for the dimensions of the shewbread: Yod, heh, zayin,
chunks.stMore: which stand for the length of ten handbreadths, the width of five handbreadths, and the height of seven fingerbreadths, respectively.

chunks.en: Ben Zoma says:
chunks.st: Ben Zoma says that it is written:

chunks.he: וְנָתַתָּ עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן לֶחֶם פָּנִים לְפָנַי תָּמִיד,
chunks.en: "And you shall put on the Shulchan lechem panim before Me always,"
chunks.st: “And you shall set upon the Table shewbread [leḥem panim] before Me always” (Exodus 25:30).

chunks.en: meaning that it should have faces.
chunks.explain: Its sides went straight up, like faces.
chunks.st: The term leḥem panim indicates that it should have vertical sides [panim] rather than a rounded shape.

summary: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Meir argue about the size of the Shulchan and how the lechem hapanim lay on it, with its ends folded up. Rabbi Meir says there was space between the two rows so the wind could blow. Abba Shaul says the bowls of frankincense were put there, and he brings a pasuk to prove it.

chunks.en: The Shulchan was ten tefachim long
chunks.st: As for the Table, its length is ten handbreadths

chunks.en: and five wide.
chunks.st: and its width is five
chunks.stMore: handbreadths, as the Torah states that the Table is two cubits long and one cubit wide (see Exodus 25:23), and Rabbi Yehuda holds that the cubit used as the unit of measurement for the construction of the Temple vessels was equal to five handbreadths.

chunks.en: The lechem hapanim
chunks.st: With regard to the shewbread,

chunks.en: were ten long and five wide.
chunks.st: its length is ten handbreadths and its width is five handbreadths.

chunks.he: נוֹתֵן אָרְכּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד רָחְבּוֹ שֶׁל שֻׁלְחָן,
chunks.en: He puts its length across the width of the Shulchan,
chunks.st: The priest places the length of the two shewbread arrangements across the width of the Table, which leaves five handbreadths of each loaf protruding from the Table.

chunks.en: and folds up two and a half tefachim on this side
chunks.st: And he folds the protruding two and a half handbreadths upward on this side of the Table,

chunks.en: and two and a half tefachim on that side.
chunks.st: and the protruding two and a half handbreadths upward on that side of the Table.

chunks.he: נִמְצָא אָרְכּוֹ מְמַלֵּא כָּל רָחְבּוֹ שֶׁל שֻׁלְחָן,
chunks.en: So its length fills up the whole width of the Shulchan.
chunks.st: One finds, therefore, that the length of the shewbread covers the width of the Table.
chunks.stMore: Similarly, since the width of each loaf is five handbreadths, the width of the two loaves filled the entire length of the Table.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yehuda says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: הַשֻּׁלְחָן אָרְכּוֹ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר וְרָחְבּוֹ שִׁשָּׁה.
chunks.en: The Shulchan was twelve tefachim long and six wide.
chunks.st: With regard to the Table, its length is twelve handbreadths and its width is six
chunks.stMore: handbreadths, as the measure of a cubit used in the construction of the Temple vessels was equal to six handbreadths.

chunks.he: לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים אָרְכּוֹ עֲשָׂרָה וְרָחְבּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה.
chunks.en: The lechem hapanim was ten long and five wide.
chunks.st: Concerning the shewbread, its length is ten handbreadths and its width is five handbreadths.

chunks.he: נוֹתֵן אָרְכּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד רָחְבּוֹ שֶׁל שֻׁלְחָן,
chunks.en: He puts its length across the width of the Shulchan,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir continues: The priest places the length of the shewbread across the width of the Table, which leaves four handbreadths of each loaf protruding from the Table.

chunks.en: and folds up two tefachim on this side,
chunks.st: He folds the protruding two handbreadths upward on this side of the Table,

chunks.en: and two tefachim on that side,
chunks.st: and the protruding two handbreadths upward on that side of the Table.

chunks.en: and two tefachim of space in the middle,
chunks.st: The width of the two arrangements of shewbread occupies only ten of the twelve handbreadths of the length of the Table, and this leaves a space of two handbreadths in the middle, between the two arrangements,

chunks.en: so that the wind can blow between them.
chunks.st: so that the wind will blow between them and prevent the loaves from becoming moldy.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says:
chunks.st: Abba Shaul says:

chunks.en: There they would put
chunks.st: There, in the space between the two arrangements, the priests would place the

chunks.he: שְׁנֵי בְזִיכֵי לְבוֹנָה שֶׁל לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים.
chunks.en: the two bowls of frankincense of the lechem hapanim.
chunks.st: two bowls of frankincense that accompany the shewbread.

chunks.en: They said to him:
chunks.st: The Sages said to him:

chunks.en: But doesn't it already say (Vayikra 24):
chunks.st: But isn’t it already stated: “

chunks.en: "And you shall put pure frankincense on the row"?
chunks.st: And you shall place pure frankincense upon [al] each arrangement,
chunks.stMore: that it may be for the bread as a memorial part, an offering made by fire to the Lord” (Leviticus 24:7)? The verse indicates that the frankincense is placed upon the shewbread and not next to it.

chunks.en: He said to them:
chunks.st: Abba Shaul said to the Sages in response:

chunks.en: But doesn't it already say (Bamidbar 2):
chunks.st: Isn’t it already stated: “

chunks.en: "And on him, the tribe of Menashe"?
chunks.explain: There "on him" means "next to him," so here too "on" can mean "next to."
chunks.st: And next to him [alav] shall be the tribe of Manasseh” (Numbers 2:20)?
chunks.stMore: Just as the preposition “alav” in this verse means that the tribe of Manasseh pitched camp next to the tribe of Ephraim and not upon it, so too, the preposition “al” means that the frankincense was placed next to the arrangements of the shewbread.

summary: Golden posts stood by the Shulchan and held up hollow rods between the loaves. Setting up or removing the rods does not push aside Shabbos, so a Kohen takes them out on Erev Shabbos. All the vessels in the Mikdash stood lengthwise along the length of the building.
stIntro: The mishna continues to describe the shewbread Table:

chunks.he: אַרְבָּעָה סְנִיפִין שֶׁל זָהָב הָיוּ שָׁם,
chunks.en: There were four golden posts there,
chunks.st: And there were four panels of gold there, which stood on the ground and rose above the height of the Table,

chunks.en: split at their tops,
chunks.st: and they split up at their upper ends, above the Table,

chunks.en: which they leaned the rods on,
chunks.st: so that the rods upon which the shewbread was placed could rest upon the panels. In this manner the panels would support the shewbread.

chunks.he: שְׁנַיִם לְסֵדֶר זֶה וּשְׁנַיִם לְסֵדֶר זֶה.
chunks.en: two for this row and two for that row.
chunks.st: There were two panels for this arrangement and two panels for that arrangement,

chunks.en: And twenty-eight rods,
chunks.st: and there were twenty-eight rods,

chunks.en: each like half of a hollow reed,
chunks.st: each of which was shaped like half of a hollow reed.

chunks.en: fourteen for this row
chunks.st: There were fourteen rods for this arrangement

chunks.en: and fourteen for that row.
chunks.st: and fourteen rods for that arrangement.

chunks.en: Neither setting up the rods
chunks.st: Neither the arranging of the rods for the new shewbread,

chunks.en: nor taking them out pushes aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: nor their removal from the arrangement of the old shewbread, overrides Shabbat.

chunks.en: Rather, he goes in on Erev Shabbos and slides them out,
chunks.st: Rather, a priest enters the Sanctuary on Shabbat eve, i.e., Friday before sundown, and removes each of the rods from between the loaves.

chunks.en: and puts them along the length of the Shulchan.
chunks.st: And according to Rabbi Meir he then places each rod in the space between the two arrangements, along the length of the Table.
chunks.stMore: Then, on Shabbat, he places the new shewbread on the Table without the rods, and he inserts the rods between the loaves at the conclusion of Shabbat. The mishna concludes:

chunks.en: All the vessels that were in the Beis HaMikdash
chunks.st: All the vessels that were in the Temple, including the Table, were placed so that

chunks.en: had their length along the length of the building.
chunks.st: their length was from east to west, along the length of the Temple.

summary: Two tables stood in the Ulam: a marble one for the new lechem hapanim and a gold one for the old, because we go up in holiness, not down. Eight Kohanim switched the old loaves and bowls for new ones, keeping bread on the Shulchan all the time. Then the frankincense was burned and the loaves were shared among the Kohanim. The mishnah also tells what happened when Yom Kippur fell on Shabbos or on Friday.

chunks.en: There were two tables in the Ulam,
chunks.st: There were two tables in the Entrance Hall,

words.note: The entrance hall in front of the Heichal.

chunks.en: on the inside, by the entrance of the Heichal,
chunks.st: on the inside of the Entrance Hall, next to the entrance to the Temple, i.e., next to the entrance to the Sanctuary.

chunks.he: אֶחָד שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ וְאֶחָד שֶׁל זָהָב.
chunks.en: one of marble and one of gold.
chunks.st: One was of marble and one was of gold.

chunks.he: עַל שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ נוֹתְנִים לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ,
chunks.en: On the marble one they put the lechem hapanim when it comes in,
chunks.st: On the table of marble, the priests place the new shewbread that has been baked, before its entrance
chunks.stMore: into the Sanctuary, so that the loaves may cool a little from the heat of the oven and not spoil.

chunks.en: and on the gold one when it goes out,
chunks.st: And when the old shewbread is removed from the shewbread Table it is placed on the table of gold upon its exit from the Sanctuary, where it remains until the frankincense is burned on the altar.

chunks.en: because we go up in holiness and do not go down.
chunks.st: The reason the shewbread is placed on a gold table when it is removed, rather than on a marble or silver table, is that one elevates to a higher level in matters of sanctity and one does not downgrade.
chunks.stMore: Since it is set on the gold shewbread Table all week, it cannot be downgraded to a marble or silver table upon its removal.

chunks.en: And there was one of gold inside,
chunks.st: And there was one Table of gold within the Sanctuary,

chunks.en: which always has the lechem hapanim on it.
chunks.st: upon which the shewbread is always found.

chunks.en: Four Kohanim go in,
chunks.st: The mishna describes the manner in which it is ensured that the shewbread is constantly on the Table: And four priests enter,

chunks.en: two holding the two rows,
chunks.st: two with the two arrangements of the new shewbread in their hands

chunks.en: and two holding the two bowls of frankincense.
chunks.st: and two with the two bowls of frankincense in their hands.

chunks.en: And four go in before them,
chunks.st: And four priests precede them, entering the Sanctuary before them,

chunks.en: two to take the two rows,
chunks.st: two to take the two arrangements of the old shewbread from the Table,

chunks.en: and two to take the two bowls.
chunks.st: and two to take the two bowls of frankincense.

chunks.en: The ones bringing in stand on the north,
chunks.st: Those bringing the new shewbread into the Sanctuary stand in the north

chunks.en: facing south.
chunks.st: and their faces are to the south,

chunks.en: The ones taking out stand on the south,
chunks.st: and those removing the old shewbread stand in the south

chunks.en: facing north.
chunks.st: and their faces are to the north.

chunks.en: These slide out and those put down,
chunks.st: These priests draw the old shewbread from the Table and those priests place the new shewbread on the Table,

chunks.he: וְטִפְחוֹ שֶׁל זֶה כְנֶגֶד טִפְחוֹ שֶׁל זֶה,
chunks.en: and each tefach of this one goes in place of each tefach of that one,
chunks.st: and for each handbreadth of this old shewbread that is removed from the Table a handbreadth of that new shewbread is placed upon the Table, so that the Table is never without loaves upon it,

chunks.en: as it says (Shemos 25):
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "before Me always."
chunks.st: “And you shall set upon the Table shewbread before Me always” (Exodus 25:30).

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: Even if these take it away and then those put it down,
chunks.st: Even if these priests were to remove the shewbread from the Table entirely, and only afterward those priests were to place the new shewbread upon the Table,

chunks.en: this too counts as "always."
chunks.st: this too would fulfill the requirement that the shewbread always be on the Table.
chunks.stMore: It is unnecessary to ensure the uninterrupted presence of the shewbread upon the Table, as long as it does not remain a single night without shewbread upon it. The mishna describes the manner in which the shewbread is distributed:

chunks.en: They went out and put them on the table
chunks.st: The priests who carried the old shewbread loaves came out of the Sanctuary and placed them on the table

chunks.en: of gold that was in the Ulam.
chunks.st: of gold that was in the Entrance Hall.

chunks.en: They burned the frankincense of the bowls,
chunks.st: The priests then burned on the altar the frankincense that was in the bowls.

chunks.en: and the loaves are shared among the Kohanim.
chunks.st: And the loaves were subsequently distributed to the priests.
chunks.stMore: This occurred on Shabbat, the day that the priestly watch that served in the Temple during the preceding week was replaced by the priestly watch that would serve during the following week. The shewbread was distributed to the priests of both watches.

chunks.en: If Yom Kippur falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: If Yom Kippur occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: the loaves are shared at night.
chunks.st: the loaves are distributed at night, at the conclusion of the fast, since they may not be eaten during the day.

chunks.en: If it fell on Erev Shabbos,
chunks.st: If Yom Kippur occurs on Friday, i.e., when the holy day begins on Thursday evening,

chunks.he: שָׂעִיר שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים נֶאֱכָל לָעָרֶב,
chunks.en: the goat of Yom Kippur is eaten at night.
chunks.st: the goat sin offering of Yom Kippur is eaten by the priests at night,
chunks.stMore: i.e., on Friday night, as it may be eaten only on the day that it is sacrificed or during the following night, until midnight.

chunks.en: The Kohanim from Bavel eat it raw,
chunks.st: And since there is no possibility of cooking the meat, as one may not cook on Yom Kippur or Shabbat, the Babylonians, i.e., priests who had emigrated from Babylonia, eat it when it is raw,

chunks.en: because they are not fussy.
chunks.st: due to the fact that they are broad-minded
chunks.stMore: with regard to their food, i.e., they are not particular and will eat meat even when it is not cooked.

words.note: They do not mind eating it uncooked.

summary: The frankincense must be on the Shulchan together with the lechem hapanim for a whole week, from Shabbos to Shabbos. If not, the loaves are pasul. If the loaves were set out late, they should be left until the next Shabbos, because staying longer does not hurt.

chunks.he: סִדֵּר אֶת הַלֶּחֶם בְּשַׁבָּת וְאֶת הַבְּזִיכִים
chunks.en: If he set out the bread on Shabbos and the bowls of frankincense
chunks.st: If one arranged the bread on the Table on Shabbat but arranged the bowls of frankincense only

chunks.he: לְאַחַר שַׁבָּת וְהִקְטִיר אֶת הַבְּזִיכִים בְּשַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: after Shabbos, and burned the bowls of frankincense on Shabbos,
chunks.st: after Shabbat, then if he subsequently burned the frankincense placed in the bowls on the following Shabbat,

chunks.he: פְּסוּלָה, וְאֵין חַיָּבִין עֲלֵיהֶן מִשּׁוּם פִּגּוּל,
chunks.en: it is pasul, and there is no punishment for it for piggul,
chunks.st: the loaves are unfit for consumption, since the frankincense had not been on the Table for the entire week. Since the burning of the frankincense did not render the loaves permitted for consumption, one is not ever liable for eating them due to violation of the prohibitions of piggul or

chunks.en: nosar, or tumah.
chunks.st: notar, or for partaking of the shewbread when one is ritually impure.
chunks.stMore: One violates these prohibitions only if the frankincense is burned in a manner that permits consumption of the shewbread.

words.note: Leftover holy food that may no longer be eaten.

chunks.he: סִדֵּר אֶת הַלֶּחֶם וְאֶת הַבְּזִיכִין בְּשַׁבָּת
chunks.en: If he set out the bread and the bowls of frankincense on Shabbos,
chunks.st: If one arranged the bread and the bowls of frankincense on Shabbat but

chunks.en: and burned the bowls of frankincense after Shabbos,
chunks.st: then burned the frankincense that was in the bowls after the following Shabbat,

chunks.en: it is pasul, and there is no punishment for it
chunks.st: that burning of the frankincense is not valid and the shewbread is unfit for consumption. And since the frankincense was not burned in a manner that permits consumption of the shewbread, one is not ever liable for eating them due to violation of the prohibitions of

chunks.en: for piggul, nosar, or tumah.
chunks.st: piggul or notar, or for partaking of the shewbread when one is ritually impure.

chunks.he: סִדֵּר אֶת הַלֶּחֶם וְאֶת הַבְּזִיכִין לְאַחַר
chunks.en: If he set out the bread and the bowls of frankincense after
chunks.st: If one arranged the bread and the bowls of frankincense after

chunks.en: Shabbos, and burned the bowls of frankincense on Shabbos,
chunks.st: Shabbat and burned the frankincense that was in the bowls on the subsequent Shabbat,

chunks.en: it is pasul. What should he do?
chunks.st: the burning of the frankincense is not valid and the shewbread is unfit for consumption. How should one act to prevent the shewbread from being rendered unfit?
chunks.stMore: One should not remove the shewbread and frankincense from the Table on the subsequent Shabbat.

chunks.en: He should leave it for the next Shabbos,
chunks.st: Rather, he should leave it on the Table until the following Shabbat, so that it remains on the Table for a full week from Shabbat to Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: It is permitted to leave the bread and frankincense on the Table beyond seven days,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ הִיא עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן יָמִים רַבִּים,
chunks.en: because even if it is on the Shulchan many days,
chunks.st: as even if it is on the Table for many days

chunks.en: there is nothing wrong with that.
chunks.st: there is nothing wrong with that, i.e., it is not rendered unfit.

summary: The two loaves are eaten two or three days after baking, and the lechem hapanim nine to eleven days after baking, because baking them does not push aside Shabbos or Yom Tov. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says it pushes aside Yom Tov but not Yom Kippur.

chunks.he: שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם נֶאֱכָלוֹת אֵין פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנַיִם,
chunks.en: The two loaves are eaten no less than two days after baking,
chunks.st: The two loaves that are brought on Shavuot are eaten by the priests no less than two days

chunks.en: and no more than three.
chunks.st: and no more than three days after they were baked.

chunks.en: How? They are baked on Erev Yom Tov
chunks.st: How so? They are generally baked on the eve of the festival of Shavuot

chunks.en: and eaten on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: and they are eaten on the day of the Festival,

chunks.he: לִשְׁנָיִם. חָל יוֹם טוֹב לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת,
chunks.en: on the second day. If Yom Tov falls after Shabbos,
chunks.st: which is on the second day. If the Festival occurs after Shabbat, on Sunday, the loaves are baked on Friday,

chunks.en: they are eaten on the third day.
chunks.st: in which case they are eaten on the third day.

chunks.he: לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים נֶאֱכָל אֵין פָּחוֹת מִתִּשְׁעָה,
chunks.en: The lechem hapanim is eaten no less than nine days after baking,
chunks.st: The shewbread is eaten no less than nine days

chunks.en: and no more than eleven.
chunks.st: and no more than eleven days after it is baked.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. נֶאֱפֶה בְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְנֶאֱכָל בְּשַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: How? It is baked on Erev Shabbos and eaten on Shabbos,
chunks.st: How so? It is generally baked on Shabbat eve and eaten on the following Shabbat,

chunks.he: לְתִשְׁעָה. חָל יוֹם טוֹב לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: on the ninth day. If Yom Tov falls on Erev Shabbos,
chunks.st: which is on the ninth day. If a Festival occurs on Shabbat eve the shewbread is baked on the eve of the Festival, on Thursday,

chunks.en: it is eaten on the tenth day.
chunks.st: in which case it is eaten on the tenth day.

chunks.he: שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
chunks.en: If the two days of Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah come before Shabbos,
chunks.st: If the two festival days of Rosh HaShana occur on Thursday and Friday, the shewbread is baked on Wednesday,

chunks.en: it is eaten on the eleventh day.
chunks.st: in which case it is eaten on the eleventh day.

chunks.en: And it does not push aside Shabbos
chunks.st: And this is because the preparation of the two loaves and the shewbread overrides neither Shabbat

chunks.en: or Yom Tov.
chunks.st: nor a Festival.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says

chunks.en: in the name of Rabbi Shimon, son of the deputy Kohen Gadol:
chunks.st: in the name of Rabbi Shimon, son of the deputy High Priest:

chunks.en: It pushes aside Yom Tov,
chunks.st: Their preparation overrides a Festival

chunks.en: but does not push aside a fast day.
chunks.explain: The fast day of Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: but does not override the fast day of Yom Kippur.
